title: Announcing the AI Engineer Network: Benjamin Dunphy

primary.label: AI Product, UX & Human Factors
primary.rationale: The talk announces the Network mobile event app and its AI-enhanced matching feature powered by a Generative Matching Algorithm (GMA) that uses LLMs to connect attendees based on their stated problems. The primary focus is on the product and how AI enhances human interaction and collaboration at events, fitting the product design and human collaboration criteria.

secondary.label: AI Platforms & Developer Tooling
secondary.rationale: Network is being open-sourced as a tool for events worldwide, positioning it as a developer-facing platform that other event organizers can deploy and build upon.

secondary.label: Retrieval, Search & Knowledge
secondary.rationale: The GMA uses LLMs and PG Vector (via Supabase) for matching attendees, which involves vector-based retrieval and search concepts, though the talk does not focus on the retrieval architecture itself.

domains.label: General Purpose
domains.rationale: The Network app is an event/conference application not tied to any specific industry vertical; it serves general-purpose event networking needs.

domains.label: Developer Platforms
domains.rationale: The app is being open-sourced for use by other events and was built for and presented at a developer-focused AI engineering conference.

summary: Benjamin Dunphy, co-founder of AI Engineer and managing partner at Software 3.0, LLC, delivers the opening welcome address at the inaugural AI Engineer Summit 2023 in San Francisco, co-hosted with Shawn "swyx" Wang. The talk functions as a product announcement keynote for the Network mobile event app and its AI-enhanced matching feature. Dunphy begins by recognizing sponsors (AutoGPT as presenting sponsor and "fastest-growing open-source project in history," Supabase as diamond sponsor, Microsoft with $13B invested in OpenAI, Fixie, and Cloudflare) and acknowledging the 500 selected attendees as experienced engineers building AI-enhanced or AI-native applications. The central announcements concern the Network app: (1) AI-enhanced matching powered by a Generative Matching Algorithm (GMA) that uses LLMs to connect attendees based on their stated problems, limited to in-person attendees, and (2) the open-sourcing of both the event app and the matching algorithm at github.com/aiDotEngineer/network. Dunphy credits lead engineer Simon Sturmer for the mobile app, Swizec Teller for the GMA, Descope for authentication, and Supabase for database and PG Vector support. The talk concludes by welcoming Swyx to the stage.
whyItMatters: The software engineering and AI concepts in this talk are tightly interconnected through the Network app's architecture. The GMA (AI concept) is implemented as an open-source project (SE concept) using a composable infrastructure stack (SE concept) that integrates vector similarity search via PG Vector in PostgreSQL (both AI and SE concepts). The full-stack TypeScript/PLpgSQL codebase (SE concept) is the medium through which the LLM-powered matching pipeline (AI concept) is realized. The AI-enhanced networking concept represents the product-level design philosophy that motivates the technical architecture. Together, these concepts demonstrate how a modern AI-enhanced product is designed, built, and distributed: starting from a human-centered problem (networking at events), applying LLMs and vector search as the AI core, selecting composable managed infrastructure (Supabase, Descope) for rapid deployment, and open-sourcing the result for community adoption. This makes the talk valuable as both a product case study and an architecture reference for AI engineering practitioners.
temporalContext: The video was published October 23, 2023, capturing the inaugural AI Engineer Summit held in San Francisco. This event occurred approximately 11 months after ChatGPT's release (November 2022), during the rapid expansion of the generative AI movement when AI engineering was crystallizing as a distinct discipline. The Summit was among the first major conferences dedicated specifically to AI engineers, preceded by swyx's foundational essay "The Rise of the AI Engineer" published on Latent Space in June 2023. The Network app's GMA represents an early production example of LLM-powered matching, predating the widespread adoption of RAG patterns and vector database tools that became mainstream in 2024. The event series subsequently grew into the AI Engineer World's Fair (3000+ attendees in June 2024) and continued expanding, reflecting the explosive growth of the AI engineering field.
takeaways: AI Engineer Summit 2023 is co-hosted by Benjamin Dunphy and Swyx, featuring two days of talks from top AI engineering founders and engineers.
AutoGPT is the presenting sponsor and was the fastest-growing open-source project in history.
Microsoft invested $13 billion in OpenAI to commercialize the AI movement and has Microsoft for Startups representatives at the event.
500 attendees were selected for the inaugural summit, all experienced engineers working with AI-enhanced or AI-native applications.
The Network mobile app now features AI-enhanced matching using LLMs to connect attendees based on their stated problems.
Network is being open-sourced, including both the event app and the generative matching algorithm (GMA).
AI-enhanced matching is currently limited to in-person summit attendees only.
Infrastructure partners include Dscope for auth and Supabase for database and PG Vector, with Simon Sturmer as lead engineer and Swyx building the GMA.

concepts.name: Generative Matching Algorithm (GMA)
concepts.explanation: A matching algorithm that uses LLMs to connect conference attendees based on their stated problems, generating personalized match explanations and talking points. The GMA takes user profiles with stated problems and uses LLMs to identify which attendees can help solve each other's problems.
concepts.importance: This is the core AI innovation announced in the talk — a novel application of generative AI to the networking/matching problem space, demonstrating how LLMs can be applied beyond text generation to facilitate human connections.

concepts.name: LLM-powered personalized matching
concepts.explanation: Using large language models to go beyond keyword or tag-based matching by understanding the semantic content of attendee profiles and generating human-readable match explanations and conversation starters.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates a practical, production use of LLMs for personalization at scale — connecting people based on semantic understanding of their needs rather than simple keyword overlap.

concepts.name: Vector similarity search for attendee matching
concepts.explanation: The GMA uses pgvector for vector similarity search, converting attendee profile data and stated problems into vector embeddings and performing similarity operations in PostgreSQL to find relevant matches.
concepts.importance: Shows a concrete production implementation of vector search for a real-world matching problem, bridging the gap between embedding-based retrieval and a user-facing product feature.

concepts.name: AI-enhanced human networking and connection
concepts.explanation: The application of AI to facilitate rather than replace human-to-human interaction — using LLMs to identify which attendees should meet and generating talking points, while the actual connection remains human-driven.
concepts.importance: Represents an important design philosophy for AI products: augmenting human capabilities (networking) rather than automating them, which is a key consideration in AI product UX design.

concepts.name: Profile-to-embedding matching pipeline
concepts.explanation: The end-to-end pipeline of converting user-stated problems and profile information into vector embeddings, performing similarity search via pgvector, and using LLMs to generate personalized match explanations and talking points.
concepts.importance: Provides a reference architecture for how raw user input flows through embedding generation, vector search, and LLM-based explanation generation to produce actionable AI-powered recommendations.

concepts.name: Open-source project release and community strategy
concepts.explanation: The decision to open-source both the Network event app and its Generative Matching Algorithm, making them freely available for any event organizer worldwide to deploy and build upon, hosted at github.com/aiDotEngineer/network.
concepts.importance: This is the central engineering decision of the talk — transitioning an internal conference tool into a community-maintained open-source project, illustrating how AI-enhanced products can be distributed and adopted beyond their original use case.

concepts.name: Composable cloud infrastructure selection
concepts.explanation: The Network app uses a composable infrastructure stack: Supabase for database and PG Vector, Descope for authentication, and cloud deployment — demonstrating how modern AI applications integrate multiple managed services rather than building everything from scratch.
concepts.importance: Shows a practical pattern for assembling AI-enhanced applications from specialized managed services, which is a key engineering decision for teams building AI products with limited resources.

concepts.name: Mobile event application architecture
concepts.explanation: The Network app is a mobile-first event application providing conference schedules, expo partner lists, recommended venues, events information, and AI-powered attendee matching — a full-featured event companion application.
concepts.importance: Provides a concrete example of a production mobile application with AI features integrated, serving as a reference architecture for AI-enhanced consumer-facing apps.

concepts.name: Full-stack TypeScript and PLpgSQL codebase
concepts.explanation: The Network repository uses JavaScript, TypeScript, and PLpgSQL, verified via the GitHub repository at github.com/aiDotEngineer/network, showing a modern full-stack development approach combining application logic with PostgreSQL stored procedures.
concepts.importance: Demonstrates a practical technology stack choice for AI-enhanced applications that combines frontend TypeScript with database-level logic (PLpgSQL) for vector operations.

concepts.name: Vector database integration with PostgreSQL via PG Vector
concepts.explanation: The app uses PG Vector (a PostgreSQL extension) within Supabase to enable vector similarity operations directly in the relational database, avoiding the need for a separate vector database service.
concepts.importance: Illustrates an architectural pattern where vector search is integrated into an existing relational database rather than adding a separate vector DB, a key design decision for teams already using PostgreSQL.

organization.name: Software 3.0 Inc
organization.summary: Software 3.0 Inc operates AI Engineer, a global conference series for AI engineers founded in 2023 by Shawn 'swyx' Wang and Benjamin Dunphy, headquartered in Oakland, CA. The organization produces flagship conferences on four continents and built the Network mobile event app with AI-enhanced matching powered by a Generative Matching Algorithm (GMA). Both the Network app and GMA were open-sourced at the AI Engineer Summit 2023. The company has approximately 11 employees and is privately held. The official privacy policy confirms the legal entity as Software 3.0, INC, headquartered at 2648 International Boulevard, 115, Oakland, CA 94601.

technologies.label: Generative Matching Algorithm (GMA)
technologies.summary: The Generative Matching Algorithm (GMA) is the core AI technique announced in the video. It uses LLMs to go beyond keyword or tag-based matching by understanding the semantic content of attendee profiles and stated problems, generating personalized match explanations and talking points. The GMA takes user profiles with stated problems and uses LLMs to identify which attendees can help solve each other's problems. The matching pipeline converts profile data into vector embeddings, performs similarity search via pgvector in Supabase, and uses LLMs to generate human-readable match explanations. This represents an early production example of applying generative AI to the human networking and connection problem space.
technologies.role: Primary AI technology announced — the generative matching algorithm that powers AI-enhanced attendee matching in the Network app, representing the core product innovation of the keynote.

technologies.label: Network (open-source event application)
technologies.summary: Network is an open-source mobile event application developed by AI Engineer, featuring conference schedules, expo partner lists, recommended venues, events information, and AI-powered attendee matching via the Generative Matching Algorithm. The app was built using TypeScript and PLpgSQL, with Supabase for database and pgvector support and Descope for authentication. Lead engineer Simon Sturmer built the mobile app while Swizec Teller developed the GMA. Both the app and its matching algorithm were open-sourced at the AI Engineer Summit 2023, making them freely available for any event organizer worldwide to deploy and build upon.
technologies.role: The overarching product being announced and open-sourced — a mobile event app with AI-enhanced matching powered by the GMA. The open-sourcing of both the app and matching algorithm is the central announcement of the keynote.

technologies.label: pgvector
technologies.summary: pgvector is a PostgreSQL extension that enables vector similarity search directly within a relational database. In the Network app, pgvector is used to convert attendee profile data and stated problems into vector embeddings and perform similarity operations to find relevant matches. This architectural pattern — integrating vector search into an existing PostgreSQL database rather than adding a separate vector DB — was an early production example that has since become mainstream for AI applications. The use of pgvector was confirmed both by the transcript (credited as 'PG Vector') and by Swizec Teller's engineering blog post detailing the GMA architecture.
technologies.role: Infrastructure component enabling vector similarity search for the GMA — credited alongside Supabase as part of the Network app's database stack.

technologies.label: Supabase
technologies.summary: Supabase is an open-source Firebase alternative providing a managed PostgreSQL database with built-in features. In the Network app, Supabase serves as both the primary database and the vector search platform through its pgvector support, enabling the GMA's embedding-based matching pipeline. Supabase was also the diamond sponsor of the AI Engineer Summit 2023, noted by Dunphy as having broken their no-event-sponsorship policy to support the inaugural summit. The use of Supabase for the Network app was confirmed by both the transcript and Swizec Teller's engineering blog post.
technologies.role: Diamond sponsor and infrastructure partner — provides database and PG Vector support for the Network app, forming the data and vector search layer of the GMA pipeline.

outcomes: Describe how LLMs can be applied to match conference attendees based on their stated problems using a Generative Matching Algorithm (GMA)
Explain the role of vector similarity search (PG Vector) and LLMs in generating personalized match recommendations
Identify the infrastructure components used in the Network app: Supabase (database and PG Vector), Descope (authentication), and their respective roles
Recognize the strategic and community value of open-sourcing an AI-enhanced product including both the application and its matching algorithm
Understand product design considerations for AI-enhanced human interaction features in event and networking contexts
challengeSeeds: Build a simplified attendee matching system using LLMs and vector embeddings to connect people based on stated problems or interests
Deploy the open-source Network app locally and trace how a user profile flows through the Generative Matching Algorithm to produce a match
Design an AI-enhanced matching feature for a different domain (e.g., mentorship platform, study group formation, job candidate matching) inspired by the GMA approach
Implement a profile-to-vector pipeline that converts user-stated problems into embeddings and performs similarity search using PG Vector or an equivalent
Audit the Network app architecture and propose improvements for scalability, user privacy, or matching quality based on the open-source code and engineering blog post
